from.place: proof: cut a perfect complex after the degree-zero fibre map is surjective

title: Local splitting after a surjective degree-zero fibre map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $K$ be a perfect object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] whose Tor-amplitude is in $[0,\infty)$. Fix a point $s\in S$ and suppose that the canonical map $H^0(K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s)\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))$ is surjective. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ and an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_U)$, $K|_U\cong H^0(K)|_U\oplus P$, where $P$ is perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood of s on which K is represented by a bounded complex of finite free modules with one term for each residue-field cohomology rank, using the finite-free residue model (Tag 0BCD). Since K has Tor-amplitude in [0,infinity), the negative-degree ranks are zero, so after shrinking the complex is concentrated in degrees >=0. The given sheaf fibre map becomes the corresponding surjection on H^0 of the localized complex.

Apply the affine cut lemma to this finite-free complex at the prime corresponding to s. It gives an element f outside that prime such that after restricting to U = Spec(R_f), K|_U is isomorphic to tau_{<=0}(K|_U) direct-sum tau_{>=1}(K|_U), and the latter is perfect of Tor-amplitude in [1,infinity).

Because K has no negative cohomology, tau_{<=0}(K|_U) is H^0(K)|_U placed in degree zero. Substituting this identification into the splitting gives K|_U isomorphic to H^0(K)|_U direct-sum P, where P=tau_{>=1}(K|_U) has the asserted perfectness and Tor-amplitude.
